cf.title: Allow table AMs to define their own reloptions

input.subject: Allow table AMs to define their own reloptions

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection questions the goal: demand has lasted since 2020 and the amoptions callback copies index AM practice. The surviving objections are fixable design points at level 2. The strongest is prior-attempts-1: the same feature was reverted twice in 2024 for design issues, and the thread never names them. replication-ondisk-2 and replication-ondisk-1 leave restore and pg_upgrade behaviour open, and maintenance-fit-1 shows a crash class that nothing catches automatically.

brief.title: Let table access methods define their own reloptions
brief.problem: Table AMs other than heap cannot define or validate their own storage parameters, and today they can only use heap's reloptions. The thread names extension AM authors as the users, and Aleksander Alekseev reports a recent commit that used a GUC for lack of this.
brief.proposed_design: The current version, Andrew Dunstan's v14, adds an amoptions callback to TableAmRoutine, in line with index AMs. AMs whose options struct starts with StdRdOptions set has_std_options_prefix, and the relcache caches this in rd_stdoptions. pg_dump moves AM-specific options to a separate ALTER TABLE ... SET entry, and ALTER TABLE takes AccessExclusiveLock for options not yet registered in the backend.
user_visible_surface: C API: TableAmRoutine.amoptions callback and has_std_options_prefix flag.
C API: add_std_reloptions_to_kind() and NUM_STD_RELOPTIONS, so an AM can accept all standard heap options.
SQL function pg_reloption_is_standard(name), planned for pg_dump in message #29.
pg_dump emits AM-specific options as a separate ALTER TABLE ... SET (...) TOC entry, which --no-table-access-method skips.
ALTER TABLE SET/RESET of an unrecognized option name now takes AccessExclusiveLock.
author_claims: The design meets most earlier objections and matches what index AMs do.
Making autovacuum AM-aware would cost a catalog lookup per relation, for a capability nothing needs.
Caching rd_stdoptions in v11 removed a small performance hit on the heap insert path.
The lock fix in v14-0001 fixes a bug that exists on master too, shown with bloom, and is probably not worth backpatching.
An extension that adds reloptions independent of the table AM is a separate project.
brief.thread_state: Andrew Dunstan posted v14 on 2026-10-27 with Rui Zhao's lock fix, and nobody has replied since. Several reviewers found bugs that later versions fixed, and no reviewer has said the patch is ready.
unclear: The v1 syntax ALTER TABLE ... SET ACCESS METHOD ... OPTIONS (ADD | SET | DROP) may or may not survive in v14.
The v1 commit says non-heap AMs lose heap reloptions, but nothing says whether AMs without amoptions keep today's behaviour in v14.
The thread does not say how existing out-of-core table AMs and their stored reloptions behave after pg_upgrade.
An AM option with the same name as a core option but a stronger lock gets the core lock, and only documentation covers this.
The thread never settles how this relates to the generic options engine in CommitFest entry 4688.
search_queries: table AM options ALTER TABLE SET ACCESS METHOD

prior_attempts.title: Reloptions for table access methods
prior_attempts.quote: The simple patch is admirable, but not something we should put into core.
prior_attempts.reason: Simon Riggs objected that not all heap options should be common to every table AM, that table and index options should work the same way, and that a behavior change needs tests, docs and code comments. Michael Paquier agreed that bypassing a sanity check is not a good long-term solution and sketched a callback-based design. Jeff Davis said he would withdraw the patch if only a fully supported feature was acceptable, and the entry was withdrawn after Simon's promised longer reply did not appear.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: That patch skipped validation so AMs could add heap-kind options. v14 uses a callback and per-AM option sets, which is the direction the objectors asked for.

objections.title: Thread does not explain how v14 avoids the 2024 revert reasons
objections.failure_scenario: A committer pushes v14, and extension AM authors build against TableAmRoutine.amoptions and has_std_options_prefix during beta. Post-commit review then finds design issues like those behind the 2024 reverts, and the feature is reverted again. Extensions built against the beta API break before release.
objections.argument: [P9] and [P12] show that custom reloptions for table AMs were committed and reverted twice in 2024 "due to multiple design issues spotted after commit", the second time per review by Andres Freund. The reverted work also touched extract_autovac_opts, and the patch still has autovacuum read StdRdOptions through the heap parser (message #17). Message #8 says the new design "meets most of the previous objections" but does not name them. None of the 39 messages, including the list of earlier attempts in message #1, mentions the reverted commits.
objections.author_must_show: Which design issues led to the 2024 reverts, and how does v14 avoid each one?

precedents.title: Revert: Custom reloptions for table AM

critic.reasoning: [P9] and [P12] record two reverts of the same feature for design issues, and no message names those issues. Message #8 says only that the design meets "most of the previous objections".

objections.title: Restore requires AM options that fix on-disk layout to be settable later
objections.failure_scenario: An AM defines an option that sets its on-disk format, such as a page or stripe layout, at CREATE time and rejects later changes. Every pg_dump restore of such a table fails at the separate ALTER TABLE ... SET entry, or the table is restored without the option and data is written in the default layout. The user finds out during a restore.
objections.argument: Message #29 moves all AM-specific options to a later ALTER TABLE ... SET TOC entry. That works only if the AM can apply its options to an empty table, and the author calls this "not ideal". Core keeps creation-time standard options such as toast_value_type in CREATE for this reason, but AM-specific options get no such path. In binary-upgrade mode the ALTER also runs before the relation files are transferred, and the proposal does not say whether an AM may write metadata into a relfilenode that is later replaced.
objections.author_must_show: How does an AM restore an option that only takes effect at creation time, both in a plain restore and in pg_upgrade's binary-upgrade mode?

critic.reasoning: Message #29 states the constraint and calls it "not ideal", so the thread confirms an AM option fixed at creation time cannot be restored. The binary-upgrade part cannot be checked without the code.

objections.title: pg_upgrade can fail when an existing table AM starts to supply amoptions
objections.failure_scenario: A columnar AM has tables with fillfactor or autovacuum_* set in pg_class.reloptions, which it accepts today through heap's parser. Its release for the new major version supplies amoptions without accepting the standard options. pg_upgrade's schema restore then runs CREATE TABLE ... WITH (fillfactor=...), gets "unrecognized parameter", and the upgrade aborts.
objections.argument: Under v14 the standard options stay in the CREATE statement (message #29), and the new AM's amoptions validates them. Message #36 only says an AM "should accept them all unless it has a good reason not to", which documentation alone cannot enforce. The proposal does not say what happens to options already stored in the catalog, and the brief lists this as unclear. Nothing makes the problem visible before the upgrade is run.
objections.author_must_show: What happens on pg_upgrade to stored heap reloptions of an out-of-core AM that newly supplies amoptions, and can pg_upgrade --check report the conflict before the upgrade starts?

critic.reasoning: Message #19 suggests AMs without amoptions keep the heap parser, so the failure needs an AM to opt in and drop standard options. Only the documentation in message #36 prevents that, and the thread does not cover stored options or pg_upgrade.

objections.title: Every core reader of rd_options must remember the rd_stdoptions guard
objections.failure_scenario: A future core patch adds a StdRdOptions field or reads rd_options as StdRdOptions in a new place, without the rd_stdoptions guard. Tests pass because heap and dummy_table_am both embed StdRdOptions. A user of an out-of-core AM that does not set has_std_options_prefix finds out from a backend crash, as in the VACUUM case in message #22.
objections.argument: The thread found unguarded readers several times: four macros (message #16), the TOAST memcpy in vacuum_rel (message #22) and RelationGetToastValueType (message #26). Reviewers found each by hand, and nothing in core fails when a guard is missing. The second test AM in message #27 only catches readers that existing tests exercise, so a new reader added later is not covered.
objections.author_must_show: What makes an unguarded read of rd_options as StdRdOptions fail at build or test time, so that a future patch cannot add one unnoticed?

critic.reasoning: Caching rd_stdoptions in v11 makes the checks agree, but each reader must still apply the guard. Messages #16, #22 and #26 show three rounds of unguarded readers found by hand, one of them a crash.

objections.title: New core reloption names can silently weaken an AM option's lock
objections.failure_scenario: An out-of-core AM registers an option at AccessExclusiveLock. A later release adds a core reloption with the same name at ShareUpdateExclusiveLock. After upgrade, ALTER TABLE in a backend that has not loaded the AM takes the weaker lock while the AM's readers assume no concurrent change, and nobody is warned.
objections.argument: Message #39 says options are matched by name across all kinds, and covers the conflict only in tableam.sgml. That puts a contract on core as well as on AM authors: every new core reloption name must be checked against an AM namespace the project cannot see. The bloom case in message #38 shows the same lock lookup already goes wrong for index AMs.
objections.author_must_show: How will core detect, at ALTER TABLE time or at AM registration, that an AM option shares a name with a core option but needs a stronger lock?

critic.reasoning: Message #39 documents the name collision, but an AM author cannot know which names core will add later. The case is narrow, and message #38 shows index AMs use the same lookup on master, so this is a question to answer, not a blocker.

refuted.title: Restore applies AM-specific options after CREATE, changing their meaning
refuted.failure_scenario: An AM adds an option that picks a layout at create time, for example a column-group setting. pg_dump creates the table without the option, then a later ALTER TABLE ... SET entry applies it. The restored table has a different layout from the source, or the ALTER fails, and the user finds out after restore.
refuted.argument: Message #29 splits AM-specific options into a separate TOC entry and requires every AM option to work when set by ALTER TABLE on an empty table. The author calls this "not ideal" and invites better ideas. Today a dump recreates reloptions inside CREATE TABLE ... WITH, and v14 changes that for every non-heap AM. The contract lives only in tableam.sgml, so an AM author who misses it finds out from a broken restore.
refuted.author_must_show: Why can pg_dump not keep all options in CREATE TABLE ... USING am WITH (...) and move them to ALTER only when --no-table-access-method is given?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-2. Message #29 also partly answers its question: pg_restore --no-table-access-method decides at restore time, so the archive needs the separate entry in every dump.

refuted.title: Stored standard options can break restore when an AM adopts amoptions
refuted.failure_scenario: An out-of-core table AM today accepts fillfactor through heap's parser. Its next release adds amoptions but does not call add_std_reloptions_to_kind(). Existing tables keep fillfactor=70 in pg_class, and a dump/restore or pg_upgrade then fails at CREATE TABLE with "unrecognized parameter".
refuted.argument: The v1 commit message says non-heap AMs lose heap reloptions unless they define them again. Messages #36 and #39 rely on documentation that an AM "should" accept all standard options. The proposal does not say how stored reloptions stay valid when an AM changes from no amoptions to its own amoptions. The brief lists pg_upgrade behaviour for existing out-of-core AMs as open.
refuted.author_must_show: What does v14 do with standard options already stored for an AM that starts to supply amoptions, and does pg_upgrade of such tables still succeed?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the pg_upgrade case more exactly. [P1] is about skipping heap validation and does not support this point.

refuted.title: A table-AM-only API may be replaced by a general options mechanism
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension that is not a table AM still cannot add WITH (...) options and keeps using a GUC, as in message #21. If core later adds a general mechanism, such as the options engine of entry 4688, out-of-core AMs that adopted amoptions and has_std_options_prefix must port to it, or core keeps both paths.
refuted.argument: Message #21 describes a real use case that this API does not serve, and message #5 argues for a generic engine. Message #24 answers that this is a separate project, but the thread does not say how amoptions and has_std_options_prefix would fit a later general design. Once extensions ship against TableAmRoutine.amoptions, core cannot remove it without breaking them.
refuted.author_must_show: How would TAM-independent reloptions or the entry 4688 engine build on amoptions and has_std_options_prefix, without a second parallel mechanism?

critic.reasoning: The amoptions callback copies the index AM practice, so a later general engine would have to convert both in the same way. Table AM extensions already adapt to TableAmRoutine changes at major versions, and message #21 describes a different feature.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Reloptions already stored in pg_class for out-of-core AMs must still pass validation during pg_upgrade's schema restore.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The patch adds the SQL function pg_reloption_is_standard(name) and changes which pg_class.reloptions values an AM accepts.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: TableAmRoutine gains amoptions and has_std_options_prefix, and reloptions.h gains add_std_reloptions_to_kind().

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: v1 to v4 add SET ACCESS METHOD ... OPTIONS (ADD | SET | DROP); the material does not show whether v14 keeps it.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump moves AM-specific options to a separate ALTER TABLE ... SET TOC entry that --no-table-access-method skips.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: see objection maintenance-fit-2: New core reloption names can silently weaken an AM option's lock

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The lock fix in v14-0001 addresses a bug that exists on master, and the author proposes not to backpatch it.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Every core reader of rd_options as StdRdOptions must apply the rd_stdoptions guard, and nothing fails when one is missing.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The heap insert path reads reloptions; v11 added the rd_stdoptions cache to remove a measured hit there.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which design issues led to the 2024 reverts recorded in P9 and P12, and how does v14 avoid each one?
How does an AM restore an option that only takes effect at creation time, in a plain restore and in pg_upgrade's binary-upgrade mode?
What happens on pg_upgrade to stored standard reloptions of an out-of-core AM that newly supplies amoptions, and can pg_upgrade --check report the conflict?
What makes an unguarded read of rd_options as StdRdOptions fail at build or test time?
Does v14 keep the SET ACCESS METHOD ... OPTIONS (ADD | SET | DROP) syntax, and do AMs without amoptions keep heap's reloptions?

committability.owner_note: Andrew Dunstan is listed as co-author and posted v14. The owner also needs to know the reloptions, relcache and pg_dump code, and should hear from the reviewer whose review led to the P12 revert.
committability.liability: A permanent TableAmRoutine callback that out-of-core AMs build against, a new pg_dump TOC entry kind, and the rd_stdoptions guard that every future reader of rd_options must apply. A third revert would break extensions built during beta.
committability.author_follow_up: Good sign: the thread reached v14 over 20 months, later versions fixed bugs that reviewers found, and v14 folds in a reviewer's lock fix.

priority.reason: The users are authors of out-of-core table AMs, but demand has lasted across attempts since 2020. The patch touches reloptions, relcache, tablecmds, autovacuum and pg_dump, and the open restore, pg_upgrade and revert-history points need answers before line-by-line review pays off.

provisional_note: Only the prose of v1 and v4 was read, not v14. Without the code, this review could not check the binary-upgrade ordering of the separate ALTER entry, whether all rd_options readers are guarded, or how AMs without amoptions behave.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch passes validate=false to fillRelOptions() for heap tables, so a custom table access method can define new reloptions of kind RELOPT_KIND_HEAP. This skips the second, hard-coded validation step that rejects such options today.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Simon Riggs objected that not all heap options should be common to every table AM, that table and index options should work the same way, and that a behavior change needs tests, docs and code comments. Jeff Davis said he would withdraw the patch if only a fully supported feature was acceptable, and the entry was withdrawn after Simon's promised longer reply did not appear.

precedents_retrieved.title: alter table set TABLE ACCESS METHOD
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an ALTER TABLE ... SET TABLE ACCESS METHOD command that rewrites a table into a different table access method, so data can be migrated between AMs without manually recreating the table. The patch also detoasted tuples in ATRewriteTable during the rewrite so that the new AM would not receive data compressed or toasted by the old one.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages show reviewers agreeing that the detoasting step in ATRewriteTable could be removed because detoasting is the table AM's responsibility, and discussing whether a dummy table AM test module would be useful; none of them gives a reason for withdrawing the entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: create table like: ACCESS METHOD
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Vik Fearing
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add an ACCESS METHOD option to CREATE TABLE ... LIKE, so that INCLUDING ACCESS METHOD (and INCLUDING ALL) copies the source table's table access method to the new table. Partitioned tables would silently ignore the option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: LIKE expands to column definitions, but the access method is a table property, so two LIKE clauses with different access methods can conflict. Its interaction with USING is also undefined. The patch overwrote any AM given in USING, and Michael Paquier asked for a clear definition of these corner cases. Peter Eisentraut argued that this syntax is the wrong approach and suggested something like USING (LIKE t1).

precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Whereas the access method is a table property.  So I don't think this syntax is the right approach for this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: New [relation] options engine
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch moves option parsing, validation and storage into one shared engine in src/backend/access/common/options.c, built on OptionSpec and OptionSpecSet descriptions. roaster_notes.note: The options-engine entries [P5] and [P7] died from inactivity, and their reason does not apply here. Message #3 raises the overlap, and other angles cover it.
Two objections above. The lock behaviour for unregistered options and the dropped v1 OPTIONS syntax were not raised, because the thread either fixed them or does not show them in v14.

The physical heap format, WAL and the wire protocol do not change. Reloptions stay text in pg_class and are parsed on relcache load, so standbys behave as they do today. The TableAmRoutine change is a normal major-version ABI break.

The proposal changes no privilege rule. Only a superuser can install a table AM with its C amoptions callback, and only the table owner can set reloptions, as today. The new AccessExclusiveLock for unregistered option names applies to the owner, who can take that lock already. pg_reloption_is_standard() reports only option names compiled into the server or registered by a loaded AM, which is not sensitive. Without the code, this review could not check that the callback runs with the owner's privileges during pg_restore.
Hot-path cost looks settled by the rd_stdoptions cache in message #32. A committer wrote the current version, which lowers the ownership risk.

Postgres has no existing way for a table AM to define and check its own per-table options: heap_reloptions rejects unknown names, and a custom GUC or a side table cannot be set or checked through CREATE TABLE ... WITH. The proposal reuses the index AM amoptions pattern rather than adding a second mechanism, and no extension does this job, so this angle finds nothing to raise.

The material shows demand that has lasted: independent attempts in 2020 [P1], 2021 [P6] and 2024 [P9, P12], plus three earlier threads cited in message #1. Rui Zhao (message #38) and Aleksander Alekseev (message #21) also want it. Alekseev's case, options set by an extension independent of the table AM, is a different feature, and the costs of this patch fall mostly on AM users. Not checked: which out-of-core AMs would adopt the callback.
